name: Lithium hydroxide monohydrate; production from spodumene concentrate; at plant; 100% purity
description:
This unit process produces lithium hydroxide from hard rock (spodumene) mineral concentrate using hydrometallurgical process. The functional unit of the process is the production of 1 kg of pure lithium hydroxide monohydrate (LiOH.H20) crystals with 2% moisture content. The gate-to-gate system boundary starts with the input of spodumene mineral concentrate with 5% Li2O and ends with the production high purity LiOH.H2O. Transport of minreal concentrate by truck and then rail has also been included. The process does not have co-products and all the environmental impacts are allocated to LiOH.H2O production.

The input mineral concentrate has 89% solids and solids have following composition by weight: Li2O:5%, Al2O3:23.5%, SiO2:66.9%, Fe2O3: 0.4%, Na2O: 0.4%, K2O: 0.6%, P2O5: 0.1% and other:3%. The input mineral concentrate undergoes numerous opreations including calciner, acid plug mixer, rotary kiln, leaching, neutralization, Ca/Mg precipitation, reverse osmosis, electrodialysis, crystalization and drying to produce high purity LiOH.H2O. Most water requirements of the process are fullfilled with recycled water and process needs energy and chemicals for multiple operations. CO2 is emitted in the calciner operation. The tails produced contains predominantly SiO2, Al2O3 and CaSO6H4, which needs to be disposed in secure tailing ponds. This process was simulated in MetSim simulation tool to generate the mass and energy balances required to calculate the inventory.

processDocumentation.timeDescription: This process was desgined based on state-of-art lithium hydroxide production from spodumene mineral concentrate. The process parameters were collected based on industrial technical reports and scientific literature from 2018 to 2022.
processDocumentation.geographyDescription: This process converts mineral concentrate (5% Li2O) from typical Canadian lithium hard rock source into high purity lithium hydroxide, and hence representiave of Canadian context. However, the process may be used in other regions, in which the composition of mineral concentrate is similar.
processDocumentation.technologyDescription: Mineral concentrate containing 5% Li2O is the feed to the Refining process. The Mineral concentrate is calcined in an direct-fired flash calciner at 1050C to convert from Alpha spodumene to Beta spodumene. The calcined feed is mixed with concentrated sulphuric acid, then heated to 250C in a rotary kiln to decompose the Beta spodumene into a leachable form. This material is then leached in mild acid (3gpl Free Acid) which solubilizes 95% of the Li into the PLS (pregnant leach solution). Hydrated lime is added to neutralize the solution and remove impurities such as iron and aluminum. Fresh Li2CO3(s) and recirculated aqueous lithium hydroxide solution, LiOH(aq), is added to remove calcium and magnesium. The purified PLS, containing 8.6 gpl Li in the form of lithium sulphate, is concentrated via the Reverse-Osmosis process to 20 gpl Li.  This solution is further upgraded and converted in the Electrodialysis process, to generate a LiOH(aq) solution containing 40 gpl Li. A portion of this LiOH(aq) is recirculated and used in the earlier process for removing Ca and Mg. The remaining PLS is fed into the Crystallization process. With an input of HP steam (1100kPa), water is flashed and lithium hydroxide is crystallized as LiOH.H2O. The flashed steam is compressed via Mechanical Vapour Compression, and re-used as heat to reduce the demand of HP steam. The solid LiOH.H2O crystals are washed, centrifuged and dried, and is the final product of the process.
processDocumentation.inventoryMethodDescription: Attributional and gate to gate process.
processDocumentation.modelingConstantsDescription: To ensure the process model is simplistic in representing a generic lithium resource, the model assumed that Spodumene is the only Li-bearing minerals. In addition, aside from Lithium, the recovery of other potential by-products such as Cesium, Tantalium, Rubidium are not considered. This unit process for lithium hydroxide monohydrate is based off a 2,000 metric ton of lithium hydroxide monohydrate production plant scale.
processDocumentation.completenessDescription:
Elementary flows are cut-off at less than 1% based on environmental relevance. Technosphere flows are cut-off at less than 1% based on environmental relevance. The mass balance for this process was calculated. The major elements that are simulated and followed in the model includes: Li, Al, Fe, K, Mn, Mg, Na, Ca.

Following elements/potential by-products are not modelled and hence are excluded from LCI
 - Cesium
 - Tantalium
 - Rubidium

The calciner operation only models major gases including CH4, O2, N2 and CO2. Hence, the formation of trace gases and particulate matter is excluded in the model and inventory.

The management/disposal of process tails, and the production and transport of chemicals and energy are excluded from gate-to-gate system boundary. It recommended to use appropriate background processes to calculate cradle-to-gate environmental impacts.

Elementary flows are cut-off at less than 1% based on environmental relevance. Technosphere flows are cut-off at less than 1% based on environmental relevance. The mass balance for this process is calculated.
processDocumentation.dataSelectionDescription: The design criteria used to build the process simulation model for the Lithium Hydrometallurgical plant is based on information obtained from technical reports publically published on various Canadian lithium hard rock deposits. Supplementary information were also obtained from journal publications, particularly for the reverse osmosis and electrodialysis processes, as these are not conventional processes used in Canada.  When information cannot be sourced, provisional estimates and reasonable process assumptions were made.  The source of the data used in the process model are clearly identified.  The process model is meant to represent the hydrometallurgical process to convert and produce lithium from a typical Canadian lithium hard rock source into high purity lithium hydroxide.
processDocumentation.dataTreatmentDescription: The tranport distances were based on average anticipated circumstances of mineral concentrate transport to refining plants in Ontario and Quebec in Canada. Mass and energy balance data from process simulation model were converted per unit mass basis of LiOH.H2O produced. Electricity consumption data all the equipments of the mill is reported as single aggregated value. Granular electricity data can be found in project publication (Kannangara et al. 2024).
processDocumentation.samplingDescription:
Boundary conditions: The gate-to-gate system boundary starts with the input of spodumene mineral concentrate with 5% Li2O and ends with the production high purity LiOH.H2O. Transport of minreal concentrate by truck and then rail has also been included.
Data collection: Data were collected from industry sources and literature.
Uncertainty: Uncertainty was not evaluated for this process.
processDocumentation.useAdvice: This process was developed to be an input to lithium hydroxide monohydrate production.

reviews.details: When available, mostly for processes pre-leaching (e.g. decrepitation, conversion and extraction), the selected process design critiera are checked against other technical reports and literatures to ensure values are reasonable and reflective of industrial operations.  For the processes post-leaching (e.g., impurity removal, reverse osmosis, electrodialysis, crystallization), the design criteria, simulated input and output are reviewed along side with the Lithium Brine simulation model, to provide cross-validation validation.  Mass and energy balance are checked on Metsim to avoid errors or non convergence in modelling.

processDocumentation.intendedApplication:
SITUATION C1 -- ACCOUNTING The intended application for this process is for accounting purposes as described in Goal Situation C1 from the ILCD Handbook’s Detailed Guidance. LCA studies with this intended application offer "purely descriptive documentation of the system under analysis (e.g., a product, sector or country), without being interested in any potential consequences on other parts of the economy.” The studies categorized under Goal Situation C1 do consider existing benefits outside the analyzed system such as recycling.

The intended application is a purely descriptive accounting / documentation of the analysed system including existing interactions with other systems in the LCI model. The target audience of this model includes LCA practitioners, industry, and the general public.
